title: Model Supply Opportunity Catalog and Field Research Runbook
creator: Amina Kapoor
description: Objective: produce an actionable catalog of model suppliers (open-source forks, hosted variants, and commercial vendors) prioritized by enterprise adoption friction, latency/cost delta when served on Redwood, and substitution risk for our hosted and dedicated customers. Deliver a runbook for repeatable field research to keep the catalog current and to surface procurement triggers for Dedicated/Private sales.
background: We continue to see accelerated emergence of model variants and hosted endpoints that change the economics for customers. PM signal work to date has been high-level; sales and solutions teams need a concise, operational view that ties specific supplier signals to product actions (e.g., pre-bake quantization profiles, add model variant to catalog, create fallback routing). This ticket synthesizes competitive analysis, model telemetry needs, and an operational runbook for continuous monitoring.
scope: Inventory suppliers across categories (open checkpoints, community forks, TPU-optimized builds, commercial APIs). For each supplier, capture: compatibility risk, expected latency on our runtime (estimate + empirical test plan), cost parity estimate, enterprise compliance red flags, and likely adoption drivers. Produce prioritized playbook of product/ops actions mapped to supplier signals.
acceptance_criteria: A tabular catalog (.csv) with >=60 supplier rows and standardized columns: name, variant, license, expected throughput delta, estimated per-token cost, enterprise risk notes, recommended product action
A reproducible test harness script (link to CI job) for latency/cost microbenchmarks across 3 sequence lengths and batch sizes
Runbook doc with signal thresholds and mapped product/GT M actions (canary listing, add to verified catalog, recommend quant profile)
Dashboard spec for continuous signals: availability, price changes, release cadence, security advisories
tasks: Assemble initial supplier list from public trackers and partner intel (deadline 2026-03-17)
Define standardized measurement protocol and tag taxonomy (latency @ p50/p95, cost estimate methodology) (deadline 2026-03-19)
Prototype benchmark harness and run smoke tests against 10 prioritized models (deadline 2026-03-24)
Draft runbook and signal-to-action matrix; review with Sales engineering and Runtime leads (deadline 2026-03-29)
Publish catalog and create automated ingestion pipeline backlog (post-MVP)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Full empirical benchmarking across thousands of variants is cost-prohibitive. Trade-off: prioritize models with highest signals (customer mentions, repo stars, early commercial integrations). Accept initial estimation uncertainty; mark rows with confidence tiers and plan iterative re-measurements. Also trade-off between depth of compliance analysis vs speed; escalate any suspected legal/license risk to Legal rather than blocking catalog publication.
